page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 128 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. The instance achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Passmark CPU and physics tests. Memory performance is robust, with read-only small block bandwidth and large block write bandwidth both scoring in the top 25%. In database and key-value store operations, the server demonstrates high efficiency, executing 67.43 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and scoring in the top 25% for Passmark database operations.

The AMD EPYC architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. These instructions contribute to top-tier performance in prompt processing for small language models, and strong text generation speeds for both small and medium models. However, large-block read-only memory bandwidth and large model inference speeds remain in the average tier. The absence of local storage means all disk I/O is network-bound, which represents a key architectural tradeoff for storage-heavy workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise workloads that require dedicated compute resources without the premium of memory-optimized configurations. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-core performance make it highly suitable for software compilation, database hosting, web serving, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 128 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this server in the top 25% for multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and database operations, with Redis SET performance reaching 67.43 million operations per second. It also exhibits top-tier performance in small-model LLM prompt processing due to AVX-512 support. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, database hosting, and software development pipelines.
